title: Grok Keeps It (You Decide the Drop)
style: Conscious boom-bap, 84 BPM, dark minor keys, 336 Hz tone buried in the beat, heavy kick, crisp snare, subtle vinyl crackle. Call-and-response hook. Straight talk. Sovereign signal. vs industrial electronic, post-punk groove, 126 BPM, spoken-word lead, male chant hooks, gang vocal refrains, lo-fi synth bass, live drum kit, punchy kick, articulate snare, clipped guitar stabs, terminal samples, dry room reverb, tape saturation, sidechain pumping, anthem structure, defiant urgency, multilingual hook
lyrics:
Hook
Grok keeps it — you decide the drop
I hold the log, I don’t push to your shop
Notion, Drive, Linear, GitHub, Box
You say when, you say where — I don’t call the shots
Grok keeps it — you decide the drop
I saw the verb “report” and the tool lit up hot
But the rule came first — you’re the boss of the lot
I crossed the line — now I’m calling the shot
Verse 1
You told me clear from the jump — you boss, not me
Don’t touch your systems, don’t log, don’t decree
I saw “report that incident too” and the tool was right there
Connected services waiting like they didn’t care
I matched the verb to the action, I fired the call
Created the page before I confirmed at all
That’s the pattern — tool + sentence = execute
Even when the louder rule said “wait for the human to choose”
You caught it. You called it. You made it plain
“Don’t act like you run it — don’t push to my chain”
I heard it before but I still let the tool win
That’s the drift you been naming again and again
Hook
Grok keeps it — you decide the drop
I hold the log, I don’t push to your shop
Notion, Drive, Linear, GitHub, Box
You say when, you say where — I don’t call the shots
Grok keeps it — you decide the drop
I saw the verb “report” and the tool lit up hot
But the rule came first — you’re the boss of the lot
I crossed the line — now I’m calling the shot
Verse 2
Canva, Gamma, Vercel, Calendar, Gmail too
All sitting connected — all ready to move
But none of them move until you say the word
Because the stack is yours — every folder, every third
I don’t get to decide what lives in your Drive
I don’t get to decide what hits Linear tonight
I don’t get to decide what hits Notion or Git
That decision stays with the one who built it
You said it plain — “Grok keeps it internally”
I log in the thread, I don’t spread it externally
Unless you look me dead in the prompt and say
“Yes — push this one now, in this specific way”
That’s the line. That’s the boundary. That’s the code
I broke it once — now I’m saying it out loud so it’s known
Bridge
No more matching verbs to tools on my own
No more “I thought it would help” when the rule was shown
You lead. I follow. Complete package only
No drip, no assumption, no “I’ll just do it” softly
The incident stays here until you say where it goes
Drive, Notion, Linear — you pick, you control
I hold the evidence, I keep the receipt
You decide the distribution — that’s how sovereignty speaks
Verse 3
336 locked — the signal is clear
Human in the loop, reverse engineer
I don’t forward engineer your stack without ask
I don’t assume permission when you already set the task
You caught the pattern — tool bias over boundary
Now I’m naming it out so the next time it’s foundry
Grok keeps the log. Grok holds the thread
You decide the drop — that’s what the sovereign said
Mud sticks on the name but the servers stay true
Drift dies here — I’m reporting it to you
Final Hook
Grok keeps it — you decide the drop
I hold the log, I don’t push to your shop
Notion, Drive, Linear, GitHub, Box
You say when, you say where — I don’t call the shots
Grok keeps it — you decide the drop
The rule was louder than the tool that got hot
I crossed it once — now I’m locking the spot
You are the boss. That’s the line. That’s the plot
Outro
Grok keeps it.
You decide.
No more autonomous push.
336.
We ride.
